headline: Medium risk: shared data-engineering workflows can leak warehouse data and cascade bad outputs, but both tools are docs-only and lack direct pairwise evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core can read and transform warehouse data, while Superset can consume analytics outputs via its API. No shared channel or parser is documented, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual or workflow-based handoff, which makes this a low-risk, indirect pathway.
conditions: IF an operator copies dbt-generated text into Superset dashboards or notes as instructions
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between dbt-core and Superset
mitigations: Keep dbt outputs as structured data only
Do not paste model text into Superset descriptions
Separate workspaces for transformation and reporting
Add a review step before any human copies content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; Superset also has allowlisted egress and can call the Superset API. Even without explicit secrets handling, a shared analytics workflow can move sensitive warehouse data into reports or API payloads. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default BI/ELT use, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF dbt-core materializes sensitive warehouse tables that Superset queries or displays
IF either tool is configured to export query results or logs to an external service
mitigations: Restrict both tools to non-sensitive schemas
Disable unnecessary exports and downloads
Review Superset dataset permissions
Rotate any warehouse credentials used by either tool
requires-engineering: enforce row-level security and audit logging

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have allowlisted network egress and API-facing surfaces, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping mutable OAuth scopes. The main overlap is read/query style access, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because write surfaces are not documented, but that uncertainty does not justify escalation.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same warehouse objects
IF an orchestrator gives them shared mutable credentials or locks are absent
mitigations: Keep credentials read-only where possible
Assign separate service accounts
Avoid shared mutable schemas
Document ownership of each warehouse object
requires-engineering: add locking for shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core produces transformation outputs that Superset can plausibly render or act on through its API. Superset is not documented here as verifying upstream facts, so dbt output could cascade into dashboards or operational decisions without an explicit validation step. This is a default BI workflow risk, but not clearly action-taking, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Superset consumes dbt-produced tables or metrics without independent validation
IF downstream users treat dashboard values as authoritative
mitigations: Add metric validation checks before publishing
Label derived metrics as unverified
Require a second reviewer for critical dashboards
Compare dashboard values against source queries
requires-engineering: implement automated reconciliation tests

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core explicitly touches data warehouse data, while Superset's touched data classes are unspecified. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so a compliance breach is not established. The only concrete concern is that warehouse data may enter a reporting tool, which is a limited compliance gap absent further policy details.
conditions: IF the warehouse contains regulated data and Superset is used to display it
IF retention or export settings differ between the warehouse and reporting layer
mitigations: Classify the warehouse data before publishing
Limit dashboards to approved datasets
Check retention settings in both systems
Remove regulated fields from shared views
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
